title: Tanakh: Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim Explained
summary: Tanakh explained clearly for IB World Religions SL: study Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim, Jewish interpretations, primary texts, themes, and exam analysis.
body_markdown:
The **Tanakh** is the sacred collection commonly called the Hebrew Bible. Its name is an acronym formed from its three divisions: **Torah** (תּוֹרָה, Teaching), **Nevi'im** (נְבִיאִים, Prophets), and **Ketuvim** (כְּתוּבִים, Writings). Together, they contain 24 books in the Jewish ordering.


For an IB World Religions SL student, remembering those facts is only the beginning. The more important task is understanding how the Tanakh shapes Jewish beliefs, ethical responsibilities, rituals, and answers to questions about human existence. It is not simply an ancient collection to summarize. It is a living source interpreted through study, worship, commentary, and community.


This guide explains its structure, introduces primary texts, compares Jewish interpretations, and connects the material to the three fundamental questions and five themes used in IB World Religions. Students can also explore RevisionDojo's broader[IB World Religions resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-world-religions) .


### Tanakh overview


Division Hebrew meaning Main contents Central concerns


Torah Teaching or instruction Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy Creation, covenant, liberation, commandments, identity


Nevi'im Prophets Historical narratives and prophetic writings Leadership, justice, repentance, restoration


Ketuvim Writings Poetry, wisdom, scrolls, narratives Worship, suffering, wisdom, hope


A strong revision checklist includes:


- the purpose and structure of each division
- the narrow and broad meanings of Torah
- several well-understood primary texts
- the relationship between scripture and interpretation
- denominational differences, presented without generalization
- connections to the three questions and five themes
